target: Motor-vehicle count in the next native source interval; per-city reporting retains original interval units
inputs: Three strictly contiguous prior source bins for the same site/direction/native interval, causal time/calendar features; graph messages only from geolocated sites within 1500m with all three identical prior timestamps and interval
splits: Ordered whole observation dates: first 70% train, next 15% validation, final 15% test (at least one date each). Three-bin histories and targets must remain within one split. No interpolation of missing records or zero filling.
calibration: Validation absolute residual split-conformal 90% intervals; finite-sample higher quantile; test coverage and width recorded without readjustment
selection: Minimum validation MAE among all candidates; no final test selection
transfer: Rotate all five: neural candidate trained using only chronological training examples of other four cities; epoch selected on only their validation examples; pooled training normalization frozen; test only held-out city's chronological test examples. No target-city fitting.
statistics: 2000 paired whole-test-date bootstrap draws for selected model versus persistence; report number of dates and wide/degenerated intervals honestly
limitations: Municipal counts may be survey samples rather than continuously observed histories
Different native intervals and collection years are not concurrent multimodal data
Geographic proximity is not a surveyed traffic-flow graph
A forecast evaluation does not independently calibrate a SUMO network
Single training seed; no automatic operational promotion
